findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. A CFPM arrived shortly into the inspection to correct. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to have one at the facility at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw eggs were oberved over both cooked and raw bacon in the standing cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was shown and moved the items to correct. Ensure that storage locations for the raw foods in the facility are maintained so that cross contamination is safe in relation to the safe cooking temperatures of the foods involved.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility could not provide test strips for the sanitizer used in the facility during the inspection. A follow-up is being scheduled for 10 days to verify compliance. Ensure that test kits are available for the sanitizer solutions in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The three part sink was observed pulling away from the wall in the kitchen and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces around moisture and food surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility does not have a way to verify the sanitizing temperature of the dish machine at the time of this inspection. Both test strips as well as a maximum registering thermometer were discussed and a follow up is being set for 10 days to verify compliance. The PIC tried showing the probe thermometer effectiveness for this situation but it could not be verified in that manner and the digital one in the facility normally used for this would not turn on. A follow up is being scheduled for 10 days.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. A CFPM arrived shortly into the Inspection to correct. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to have one at the facility at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area/front was without a hand drying provision. Paper towels were supplied during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote good hand washing practices in the facility.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility does not have a way to verify the sanitizing temperature of the dish machine at the time of this inspection. Both test strips as well as a maximum registering thermometer were discussed and a follow up is being set for 10 days to verify compliance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use on the surfaces in the facility. The PIC had a sani bucket prepared using quat to correct. Ensure that there is a sanitizer available for use at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Yogurt is observed in the display cooler in the bar area at 45 degrees. A discussion took place with the PIC and the yogurt discarded to correct. The cooler was also adjusted colder to ensure future TCS foods are maintained safe.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) Multiple containers to the left of the microwave used for storing utensils are soiled with food debris. 2) These same containers also have a phone charger hanging across the top and in contact with the utensils. This is not considered a clean surface. The charger was remained and the utensils/ containers moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Facility does not have signed reporting agreements on file. Inspector provided a blank reporting agreement to be copied and reviewed with staff. Keep signed copies on file as verifiable proof that staff have been educated on foodborne illnesses and symptoms. CORRECTED- PIC printed reporting agreements and had employees sign them.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
--Multiple cartons of liquid egg whites (one opened and 3 unopened in the kitchen cooler, ~11 unopened in the storage cooler) with manufacturer use-by dates of 8/29/2022. One unopened carton in the storage cooler observed with a use-by date in June 2022. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC, who voluntarily discarded all expired cartons of egg whites.
--Opened gallon of milk in the barista cooler observed with a manufacturer use by date of 12/4/2022. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Milk was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No food protection manager certificates could be provided. One PIC is in the process of enrolling for the course, while the other could not locate his certificate. Ensure sufficient CFMs on staff to cover all times of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels present at the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED— Sink supplied with paper towels.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Several open half-gallons of milk observed in the bar/coffee prep cooler without date marking. CORRECTED— Staff stated that containers were opened yesterday, and labeled containers indicating this.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee return to kitchen assisting customers and don gloves without washing hands before putting on gloves. CORRECTED- Provided education and discussed with employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; (P)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed cut melon on the top shelf of white mini fridge to be 47F (probed). CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, fruit cups were voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A)(2) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained at 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed egg products in kitchen cooler without date markings. CORRECTED- PIC stated that items were received on 5/21. Items were labeled with appropriate dates.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed single service plastic utensils for customers stored in such a way that allows contamination of eating ends when utensils are picked up. Utensils must be stored all going the same direction, allowing one utensil to be picked up without touching the eating-end of other utensils.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. (C)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the cooler in the kitchen to be at 58F upon initial inspection. An employee had just been rearranging the cooler. The cooler was shut and allowed to rest for 20 minutes prior to checking again. Air temperature in the cooler was at 54F at the 20 minute mark and the yogurt sitting directly below the blower was at 46.8F when probed. Facility was instructed to have the cooler worked on. Eggs and raw bacon in the cooler were discarded. Yogurts were allowed to be moved to another working cooler. The cooler had been checked this morning at 5:40 AM and was at 38F. Ensure that the coolers are regularly checked throughout the day to ensure they are still in proper working order. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Ensure that the mop sink is caulked to the wall to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. This will prevent water and debris from falling around the mop sink in areas that cannot be accessed to clean. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the cooler in the kitchen to have a quart of pooled eggs that were dated for the day they came in, but were not dated with the date they were opened. Also, observed a container of "cheese for toast" in the same cooler that was had "Good thru 01/17/2017" written on the wrap. Ensure that PHFs are date marked within 24 hours of opening and discarded after 7 days. Cheese was discarded during the inspection and manager stated the eggs would have been opened this morning. Manager was allowed to date mark the eggs.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed a dirty bacon box in the cooler in the kitchen. The lid had been open on the box allowing for numerous amounts of sauces and other food products to spill into the bacon. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Manager removed the bacon from the cooler and discarded it.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed plastic containers at the bar that were holding individual sugars and other food products, as well as single service. Ensure that these items are rotated up to a higher plastic container level so that they are 6 inches off the floor. 
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the inside base of the cooler in the kitchen to have an accumulation of dirt and debris. 2) Also, observed the fryers in the kitchen to have an accumulation of grease and food debris on the outside of them. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed a single service spoon sitting in the salsa in the drawer cooler at the bar. There is no food service occuring at this time. Ensure that single service articles are not reused.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed a mop bucket by the mop sink to be filled with dirty water. Mop water is considered waste water and should be emptied following each use to avoid attracting pests. Manager emptied mop water during inspection.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back outer door by dry storage to have visibile sunlight coming in around multiple edges. Manager states that maintenance is on site, but does not believe that they will be able to repair the door today. Ensure that allow outer openings are self-closing and tight fitting.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the drain at the 3 compartment sink in the kitchen to be soiled. Ensure that floors and drains are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state to prevent pests.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following walls, ceilings, and attached equipment to be soiled or in disrepair: 1) The mop sink has a gap between the basin and the wall that is not easily cleanable. To fix this, the sink should be caulked to the wall to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 2) The caulking at the 3 compartment sink has become removed. Recaulk the sink. 3) Observed a table across from the 3 compartment sink that is attached to the wall without caulking to the wall. Caulk the table to the wall to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 4) The wall next to the fryer has an excessive accumulation of grease and dirt. Clean the walls by the fryer. 5) The hand sink in the kitchen has caulking that is in disrepair. Recaulk the hand sink. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a mop resting in the mop sink. Ensure that mops are stored either inverted or hanging to allow for sufficient air flow to drip dry. 
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 800: Observed a fly swatter on an unused drainboard over the dish machine on the frontline. Moved during the inspection. Drainboard should go through the dish machine to eliminate potential for cross contamination.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 850: Observed the wall mounted knife block in the kitchen to be soiled. Remove and clean the holder.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 1060: Observed the handsink in the kitchen to have mismarked H and C faucets. Hot is properly located on the left side, the faucet is marked for cold water. Switch the faucet handles.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed containers of chicken and ham that had not been date-labeled when they were re-portioned in new containers. Observed dairy product containers (liquid eggs and cream) that were not dated as to when they were opened. 
Properly label all containers of PHF with date labels. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink on the counter in the food prep area, and a container of employee food in the reach in cooler.
Employees should consume food only in the proeprly designated area, and should nstore personal food items segregated from commmercial food products.
CORRECTED = Food containers were removed and discarded.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wash, rinse water clean, proper temperature
findings.comment:
Observed that the dish washing machine in the bar area was not able to reach proper sanitizing temperatures. The machine was tested with a "T-Stick" temperature testing device, and the reading was below the minimum temperature. The unit will be serviced by a technician. In the meantime, the dish washing machine in the adjacent kitchen area will be used to wash and sanitize the glassware from the bar. 
CORRECTED = The establishment will substitute the other dish machine for this unit, until repairs are completed. A spot check will be done by inspector in the next few weeks to verify repairs.
750-830 Machines using hot water for sanitizing may be used provided that wash water and pumped rinse water be kept clean and water shall be maintained at not less than the temperature stated for that machine. Single-tank, stationary rack, dual-temperature: wash temperature 150°F.  Single-tank, stationary-rack, single-temperature machine:  wash temperature 165°F.  Single-tank, conveyor machine wash temperature: 160°F.  Multi-tank, conveyor machine wash temperature: 150°F.  Multi-tank, conveyor machine pumped rinse temperature: 160°F.  Single-tank, pot, pan and utensil washer (either stationary or moving rack): wash temperature 140°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the wall-mounted knife holder had some dust and debris along the top of unit.
Clean this equipment.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a spray bottle in the bar area that was labeled "bleach", but the bottle contained air freshener. 
Label all bottles of liquids with the proper name of the liquid within.
CORRECTE = Bottle was relabeled properly.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed that the container for holding wiping cloths in sanitizing solution in the bar area was at a concentration of 0ppm. This solution was discarded, and a new solution made that was was tested to 400ppm of Quaternary ammonia in solution. The first solution had lost its concentration over time and needed to be replaced.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.
Provide sanitizing solution of proer concentration to sanitize surfaces as needed. 
CORRECTED= new solution was made.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed that there is a leak in the plumbing from the dish washer unit in the kitchen.
750-1100(b) Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.
Repair the plumbing in the dish machine. 
NOTE** the repair technician was working on the system during the inspection.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floors under the prep table in the kitchen are soiled. 
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
See Voluntary Destruction Form - 
[1] Deli-sliced ham (~3/4 lb), and shredded cheese (~1/2 of a 5lb bag) were found in kitchen cooler with dates of 10/31 and 10/29, respectively.  CORRECTED - both items were immediately, voluntarily discarded by manager.  While facility appears to do an excellent job with date-marking, staff need to make sure that foods are discarded after 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
[2]  Four sandwiches, shredded cheese, pizza sauce and sour cream were found in low boy cooler drawers (under prep cooler) at temperatures 50-52 degrees F (probe).  CORRECTED - manager immediately, voluntarily discarded these items.
[3]  9 individual portions of cream cheese, and ~50 packets of butter were found in the top portion of the prep cooler at temperatures 49-52 degrees F (probe).  CORRECTED - staff immediately, voluntarily discarded these items.
[4]  Milk, Greek yogurt, half-and-half, yogurt, silk, whipped cream, cups of cut fruit containing cut melons were found in small coffee cooler at temperatures 48-52 degrees F (probe).  CORRECTED - staff immediately, voluntarily discarded all out of temperature items.
All items from part 2, 3, and 4 were initially checked with the laser thermometer, then probed with stem thermometer and left within cooler, with lid closed, for a short time.  The coffee cooler items were checked after 45 minutes of keeping door closed.  See Violation #4.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
[1] Bistro prep cooler was found incapable of holding foods below 41 degrees (in low boy drawers, and in top portion).  Air thermometer in top portion of prep cooler reads 48-50 degrees F.  All potentially hazardous foods were immediately removed.  Cooler must not be used for holding potentially hazardous foods until after follow-up in two weeks.
[2]  Small bistro cooler appears to be 48-52 degrees throughout cooler.  Thermometer at front of cooler reads 48 degrees F.  Staff and inspector kept cooler closed for 45 minutes and checked again.  Temperatures had not fallen.  All potentially hazardous foods were immediately removed.  Cooler must not be used for holding potentially hazardous foods until after follow-up in two weeks.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Ice scoops in kitchen were stored on top of ice machine, in bowl with slight amounts of food debris, and deli paper.  CORRECTED - bowl was set for washing and deli paper was removed.    Ice scoops shall be stored on a smooth and easily cleanable surface, or in the ice with the handle extended.
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Interior ceiling of microwave is soiled.  Wash, rinse, sanitize, and maintain this surface to eliminate potential for cross-contamination.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
The containers of spatulas and utensils by the toaster in the kitchen are soiled (REPEAT).  CORRECTED - manager immediately placed containers and utensils into line for being washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
(A) Coffee filters are observed uncovered and stored atop the coffee machine (REPEAT).  Store filters in a way that protects them from contamination.
(B) Two cases of napkins/paper towels are stored on the floor in the back storage room.  Store these items at least 6 inches off of floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
There were no paper towels available at the bistro hand sink (REPEAT).  CORRECTED - staff obtained a small stack of paper towels and placed them at hand sink.  Do not use sani-cloths for hand drying.  Stock paper towels at hand sinks at all times.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
